newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: United Nations leave broad Iraq sanctions in place.
newsitem.headline: United Nations leave broad Iraq sanctions in place.

text.p: The United Nations Security Council on Friday voted to keep in place broad economic sanctions imposed on Iraq since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The decision was expected and means the ban on the export of Iraqi oil and on most imports, except for food medicine and other humanitarian items, will not be lifted.

A key condition for any lifting of the broad sanctions, which are separate from a deal Iraq signed with the United Nations last May for a partial humanitarian lifting of the ban on oil sales, is a clean bill of health by the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of eliminating Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.

UNSCOM's chairman, Rolf Ekeus, must be satisfied that Baghdad has discolsed full details of its nuclear, chemcial, biological and ballistic missile programs and that forbidden weapons and facilities have been scrapped.

However, U.S. ambassador to the U.N., Madeleine Alrbight said after hearing Ekeus's briefing to the Security Council on Friday that "Iraq's pattern of defiance toward the U.N. special commission continues unabated."
